bottom_line: In survivors of acute myocardial infarction with clinical evidence of heart failure, ramipril vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality by 27% (95% CI 11% to 40%).
implications: These data support that, in this selected post-AMI population with clinical evidence of heart failure, allocation to ramipril (vs placebo) was associated with lower all-cause mortality (170/ramipril vs 222/placebo; 27% risk reduction, 95% CI 11% to 40%) and a lower risk of the prespecified first validated composite outcome (19% reduction, 95% CI 5% to 31%). The document also reports more hypotension with ramipril (42 [4-2%] vs 23 [2-3%]) and does not provide evidence here to conclude a clear effect on reinfarction or stroke because event numbers were small.

major_points.text: Multicentre, multinational, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial in post-AMI patients with clinical evidence of heart failure.
major_points.quote: The AIRE Study were described prospectively.4 In brief it was a multicentre, multinational, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study. 2006 patients with acute myocardial infarction and clinical evidence of heart failure

major_points.text: Patients were randomly allocated to placebo (992) or ramipril (1014), started in hospital between day 3 and day 10 after AMI.
major_points.quote: randomly allocated to double-blind treatment with either placebo (992 patients) or ramipril (1014 patients) on day 3 to day 10 after AMI (day 1).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was all-cause mortality analysed by intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote: The prespecified primary statistical endpoint was all-case ("intention-to-treat"), all-cause mortality.

major_points.text: Secondary composite (first validated event: death, severe/resistant heart failure, myocardial infarction, or stroke) was reduced by 19% (95% CI 5% to 31%; p=0.008).
major_points.quote: death, severe/resistant heart failure, myocardial infarction, or stroke (95% CI 5% to 31%; p=0·008).

major_points.text: Syncope and hypotension were more common with ramipril than placebo.
major_points.quote: Syncope was reported for 24 (2-4%) patients on ramipril and 17 (1-7%) on placebo with a similarly increased occurrence of hypotension in the ramipril treated group-42 (4-2%) compared with placebo 23 (2-3%).

guidelines_referenced.text: European Guidelines for Good Clinical Research Practice
guidelines_referenced.quote: ensure that the study conduct adhered closely to the European Guidelines for Good Clinical Research Practice.

inclusion_criteria.text: Aged at least 18 years admitted with a definite AMI and clinical evidence of heart failure at any time after the index AMI.
inclusion_criteria.quote: All patients aged at least 18 years admitted to coronary care, intensive care, or general medical units with a definite AMI and clinical evidence of heart failure at any time after the index AMI

exclusion_criteria.text: Severe heart failure (usually NYHA grade IV).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients with severe heart failure (usually NYHA grade IV)

exclusion_criteria.text: Heart failure of primary valvular or congenital aetiology.
exclusion_criteria.quote: heart failure of primary valvular or congenital aetiology

exclusion_criteria.text: Any recognised contraindications to ACE inhibitor treatment.
exclusion_criteria.quote: any of the recognised contraindications to ACE inhibitor treatment were excluded from the study.

criticisms.text: Most patients were followed for less than 18 months; curves were terminated at 30 months because of small numbers with prolonged follow-up.
criticisms.quote: Most patients were followed for less than 18 months, and the curves have been terminated at 30 months because of the small numbers of patients with prolonged follow-up.

criticisms.text: A substantial proportion were no longer taking randomised medication by 18 months, and many withdrawn from placebo were taking open-label ACE inhibitor.
criticisms.quote: by 18 months 40% of patients (excluding those who had already died) were no longer taking randomised medication and that most of the patients withdrawn from placebo were taking open-label ACE inhibitor.

criticisms.text: The incidence of stroke was higher in the active drug group but numbers were small, so an adverse effect could neither be supported nor refuted.
criticisms.quote: The incidence of stroke was higher in the active drug group but the numbers were small and an adverse effect of the drug can be neither supported nor refuted.
